reason: Round-4 objection resolved. The line is now the dative NP alone (diwéy ph₂tréy). The verb is gone: its o-grade causative came from the support ref Cato Agr. 83.1, and Umbr. vufru is an adjective. `secure` lists only the two nouns, both exact in Gk and It per the builder. Loci re-checked: Il. 17.498 and Od. 13.51 εὐξάμενος/-οι Διὶ πατρί (AGDT: DAT SG, OBJ + ATR) and Il. 24.287 σπεῖσον Διὶ πατρί; Tab. Ig. IIb 7 Iuve patre fetu, IIb 22-23 sestu Iuvepatre, IIb 26 fetu Iuvepatre, and IIb 17-18 Iuvepatre prepesnimu (support), all in the Buck OCR. Buck's glossary gives dat. sg. Iuvepatre 5 times and Iuve patre at IIb 7. PIE against daughters: diwéy ph₂tréy matches Διί πατρί cell for cell. Umbr. Iuve has the analogical full grade, as Lat. Iovī does. IIb 7 writes the two words apart, and both members are inflected, so the Umbrian is a syntagm, not a compound. Both branches have the dative in ritual address (an offering or prayer to the god). Caveats: Cato Agr. 134.1 (Iano Ioui Iunoni, LASLA) carries *dyḗws only and belongs in support. But it is the ref through which the builder credits *dyḗws to Italic, since Umbr. Iuve is in no table, so the clean fix is a table key for Iuve, not just a role change. This is the same formula as sky-father-001/-003, in another case.

Round-4 objection resolved: the line is cut to the NP, as r4 proposed. The verb stitched from the plural-object RV 10.123.7 is gone, and so is 'begot', which fit neither text. priHóm h₁nómn̥ (ACC SG n.) matches RV 10.84.5c priyáṃ te nā́ma (VedaWeb ACC SG, object of gr̥ṇīmasi) and Crist 636 freónoman (acc. sg., object of cende). Both have adjective before noun (OE as a compound). The builder finds both members exact: frēo < *frijaz < *priHós, and nama. Loci re-checked: RV 10.84.5c, 10.123.7d (nā́ma … priyā́ṇi, ACC PL) and 7.56.10a (priyā́ vo nā́ma, ACC PL) in VedaWeb; Crist 636 in Grein, Bibliothek I. Grein's apparatus has notes on 635, 641, 642 and 647 but none on 636, so freónoman is the manuscript reading. Caveats: Grein's Sprachschatz files Cri. 636 cende under cennan 2 'creare, facere' and glosses freó-nama as 'cognomen'. The OE sense is therefore 'by-name, surname'; 'dear' is the Vedic sense, and Scheller's is 'own'. OE has a compound where Vedic has a syntagm (with te between the words in the singular locus). The OE witness is a Christian poem, and Schmitt §97 calls the pair an idiom, not necessarily poetic phraseology. Stale note (r2 P10 pattern): the support ref says the OE Bede is not local. It is: oe-bibliothek-ags-prosa, Bibliothek der ags. Prosa IV, has 'wæs his freonama Oesc' for Bede 2.5 cognomento Oisc. The ref should be cited as checked.

The fix resolves r4's mechanical objection only. The interpolated verb ǵʰuHéyeti is gone, and the accusative plural follows both parallels: RV 10.65.15 (= 10.66.15) devā́n … amŕ̥tān (VedaWeb ACC PL, object of vavande) and Plaut. Amph. 1093 deos inmortalis (LASLA ACC PL, object of inuocat). Both were re-checked, as were the support refs RV 3.4.11 devā́ḥ … amŕ̥tāḥ and Cato Orig. 4 fr. 7 dii immortales. The substantive r4 objections cannot be fixed in a plan, and they stand: (1) only *deywós is shared in the same formation; Lat. in-mortālis is a new formation, root-level, and the builder finds no path for it; (2) 'immortal gods' is a near-universal pairing (P5); (3) Plautus adapts a Greek original, so di immortales there may render ἀθάνατοι θεοί. Form: the engine's n̥mr̥tóns is oxytone, against Ved. amŕ̥tān, the only exact witness (r4 minor point, still open). The engine also prints the adjective first (n̥mr̥tóns deywóns), where both daughters put the noun first (devā́n … amŕ̥tān, deos inmortalis).

At the reject edge, as in r4. The fix sets the case to ACC (no change in print: for the neuter, nom. = acc.) and now cites Hesiod as local. That resolves r4's case and stale-note points, not its verdict. Loci re-checked: RV 3.2.7 ā́ svàr mahát (VedaWeb: svàr SG, mahát SG of mahā́nt-, objects of ā́ … apr̥ṇat beside ródasī) and Hes. Th. 19 Ἠέλιόν τε μέγαν (glaux 0020-001, OBJ_CO + ATR); the support ref RV 2.23.2 sū́ryaḥ … maháḥ was checked too. Neither member is the same formation in both branches. 'Great' is exact in Greek only: mahát is the nt-stem, and the builder now tags it as an erratum and gives level root. 'Sun' is credited in Vedic only: ἠέλιος, a -io- derivative, has no key, so its level is none. Ved. svàr in this pāda is a region Agni fills beside the two world-halves, not the Sun as a figure, and its zero-grade root is not the engine's o-grade sóh₂wl̥ (levelled ablaut, the same caveat accepted elsewhere, not a verdict point). 'Great' is the most generic of epithets (r2 P5). The engine prints méǵh₂ sóh₂wl̥, adjective first, where both cells put the noun first (svàr mahát, Ἠέλιόν … μέγαν). A plan cannot fix any of this; keep the line out of eval or drop it.

At the reject edge. The fix sets the case to ACC, so the printed sóh₂wl̥ spéḱm̥ now follows both cells: RV 4.13.3 tám sū́ryam … spáśam (VedaWeb ACC SG, objects of vahanti) and Hymn. Dem. 62 Ἠέλιον … σκοπὸν (glaux 0013-002, OBJ + APOS), both re-checked. Hymn. Dem. is now cited as local, and the apposition is faithful. The r4 objection stands, and a plan cannot fix it: no word is the same formation in both branches. Sun: sū́rya- and ἠέλιος are both derivatives. The builder now tags sū́rya- as an erratum (level root) and has no Greek path (level none). If both are -io- derivatives of the l-stem (*suh₂l-io- / *sāwel-io-), they share a formation, but it is not the engine's base heteroclite sóh₂wl̥, which stands in neither cell. Watcher: the root noun spáś- against the o-grade thematic σκοπός is root level only. The distinctive part of the parallel, the genitive of what is watched (víśvasya jágataḥ / θεῶν … ἀνδρῶν), has no cognate pair and is rightly left out. What remains is a motif carried by root-cognates; West ch. 5 claims only that σκοπός 'has the same root as spáś-', so the scholarly claim is root-level, not formulaic.

Both r4 objections are resolved. 'Gods' (the interpolated θεοί) is gone, so the line is the secure head plus dependent. The agent noun is now the suffix-accented *dh₃tḗr (NIL *dh₃-tér-, with Ved. dātár- and Gk δοτήρ as evidence), the accent type of every cited cell. Loci re-checked: Od. 8.325 θεοί δωτῆρες ἑάων (AGDT: NOM PL SBJ_AP + GEN PL), Y. 65.12b vohunąm dātārō (CAB) and RV 8.51.5 dātā́ vásūnām (VedaWeb NOM SG + GEN PL). West ch. 3, after Benfey 1872 and Schmitt 1967 pp. 142-8, says the phrases 'must go back to a common prototype'. Caveats on form: (1) The engine's zero-grade root dh₃- is NIL's, and Greek attests it in δοτῆρες (Il. 19.44 σίτοιο δοτῆρες, AGDT; not cited). The cited cells have the full grade: δωτῆρες by contamination with δώτωρ, Indo-Iranian dā- generalized. The root ablaut is levelled in all three cells, not contradicted by a competing type, and citing Il. 19.44 as support would document the form. (2) The gen. pl. h₁uséwōm is the proterokinetic weak stem. Ved. vásūnām and Av. vohunąm have the root-accented full grade, and Hoffmann (West n. 43) derives ἑάων from *h₁wéswōm. Whether that is levelling or an acrostatic paradigm is an engine/lexicon question. (3) In Y. 65.12 the Aməṣ̌a Spəṇtas are addressed (nom. = voc. pl.), and Vedic has the singular. (4) The builder gives the head pie-lex-dh3texr level none, because dātar- routes to *déh₃tōr and δωτήρ and dātár- reach no suffix-accented id. That is a mapping false negative, not evidence against the line. h₁wésu- is exact.

The r4 leak is resolved. The possessive is now enclitic 'my' (moy, after the first word), as in RV 1.164.33 dyaúr me pitā́ … bándhur me mātā́ pr̥thivī́ (VedaWeb: me GEN SG in both halves; re-checked), so it no longer comes from the uncited AVP 5.21.1. The rest of r4 stands. Outside Vedic only the kin terms are shared. Lucr. 1.250-251 Pater aether … Matris terrai (LASLA, re-checked) is a Greek philosophical topos, a derivative witness, and not a nominal sentence. The OE Æcerbot is not in the local corpora (I searched Grein, Sweet and Bright and did not find it), and its folde is root-level. The builder credits *dyḗws in Vedic only (level none). The engine still prints pl̥th₂éwih₂ against Ved. pr̥thivī́ (P6, outside the plan). Stale note: Varro RR 1.1.5 is local (latin-ogl-latin phi0684.phi002: 'Iuppiter pater appellatur, Tellus terra mater'). It is the only Latin passage with Iuppiter + pater + mater, but it is antiquarian etymologizing, and West doubts its antiquity, so the support role is right; the note's 'not in local corpora' is wrong. Minor: the -kʷe between the clauses has no counterpart in RV 1.164.33, which is asyndetic across the pādas; AVP 5.21.1 has ca … ca.

Two of r4's three objections are resolved. 'Of the gods' is dropped: it was stitched from RV 1.185.6, where jánitrī is the ACC DU of Heaven and Earth (re-checked). The agent noun is now the suffix-accented ǵenh₁tḗr, as Ved. janitā́ in the cited stanza. The printed dyḗws ph₂tḗr ǵenh₁tḗr now matches the Vedic NP cell for cell (RV 4.1.10 dyaúḥ pitā́ janitā́, VedaWeb NOM SG three times, re-checked; also 1.164.33). The third objection is structural, and it stands. The only second branch is Catull. 64.26-27 Iupiter ipse, ipse … diuum genitor (LASLA, re-checked). Its 'father' is only inside the name: the builder gives ph₂tḗr level none, and genitor level root via the -tor- lexeme, though genitor has the same suffix (Latin generalized -tor- and cannot show which accent type it continues). The poem is a Hellenistic-modelled epyllion, and diuum genitor varies the Ennian divom pater type. Under r4 rule 3 a derivative witness is only a caveat when the line stands without it, and this line does not. Remedy: the parallel the literature names is West ch. 2's pitā́ janitā́ 'father begetter' pair, with Av. Y. 44.3 ząθā ptā (CAB), Eur. Ion 136 Φοῖβός μοι γενέτωρ πατήρ (glaux 0006-010) and Enn. Ann. 113 Vahlen (= 108 Sk.) o pater o genitor (Vahlen local; Cicero's text has genitor, most Lactantius MSS lack it, add. Pal.). All are uncited and all local, and none is of Dyaus. A line *ph₂tḗr ǵenh₁tḗr on those loci (II + Gk + It) would be the honest one, with Dyaus Vedic-only or left out.
